'''Izu no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (''izu no kuni no miyatsuko'', ''izu kokuzō'') was a {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} who ruled {{ill|Izu Province|ja|伊豆国}}.

== Overview ==

=== Ancestry ===
*According to the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'', '''{{ill|Wakatakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|若建命}}''', eighth-generation descendant of Amenunuboko-no-Mikoto, ancestor of the {{ill|Mononobe-no-Muraji|ja|物部氏|lt=Mononobe-no-Muraji}}, was appointed Izu no Kuni no Miyatsuko during the reign of {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}}.
*According to the shrine tradition of Hihayoamatsu Shrine, the distant ancestor of the Izu no Kuni no Miyatsuko, Karihayasu-no-Take-Hihayo-no-Mikoto, was the eldest son of '''{{ill|Mishima-Mizokui-mimi-no-Kami|ja|三島溝橛耳神}}'''.

=== Clan ===
The original clan name and rank of the kuni no miyatsuko are unknown, but they are presumed to have been '''{{ill|Izu clan|ja|伊豆氏}}''' (''izu-uji''; {{ill|kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} of {{ill|Atai (kabane)|ja|直 (姓)|lt=Atai|lt_ja=直}}).

== Base ==
Unknown, but the construction of kofun first began (late {{ill|5th century|ja|5世紀}}) in what later became {{ill|Tagata District|ja|田方郡}}.<ref>Shizuoka Prefecture, "Chapter 1: The Formation of Primitive Izu Province within the Unification of the Archipelago (Yayoi period – 6th century)" [https://www.pref.shizuoka.jp/soumu/so-430a/kenminnohi/chapter1.html]</ref>

=== Territory ===
The whole of later '''{{ill|Izu Province|ja|伊豆国}}''' — present-day {{ill|Izu Peninsula|ja|伊豆半島}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|ja|静岡県}}.

== Tutelary deity ==
Possibly '''{{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}}''' (''mishima taisha''), the {{ill|ichinomiya|ja|一宮}} of {{ill|Izu Province|ja|伊豆国}}, located in the former {{ill|Tagata District|ja|田方郡}}. The {{ill|shake|ja|社家|lt=hereditary priestly house}} was the {{ill|Yatabe clan|ja|矢田部氏}}, descendants of the kuni no miyatsuko.

=== Tombs ===
*'''{{ill|Mukōyama Kofun Cluster (Mishima)|ja|向山古墳群 (三島市)|lt=Mukōyama Kofun Cluster}}'''
*:A {{ill|kofun cluster|ja|古墳群}} in {{ill|Mishima, Shizuoka|ja|三島市|lt=Mishima City}}, comprising 2 {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|ja|前方後円墳}} and 14 {{ill|round mounds|ja|円墳}}. The 21-meter-long keyhole-kofun Mound 3 dates to the {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}}, and the 68-meter-long Mound 16 dates to the {{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀}}.
*'''{{ill|Hyōtanyama Kofun (Kannami)|ja|瓢箪山古墳 (函南町)|lt=Hyōtanyama Kofun}}'''
*:An 87-meter-long keyhole-shaped kofun in {{ill|Kannami, Shizuoka|ja|函南町|lt=Kannami Town}}, dating to the early Kofun period ({{ill|4th century|ja|4世紀}}).
*'''{{ill|Komagata Kofun|ja|駒形古墳}}'''
*:A keyhole-shaped kofun in {{ill|Izunokuni, Shizuoka|ja|伊豆の国市|lt=Izunokuni City}}, dating to the late Kofun period. The forward portion has now been leveled, but a long sword was once excavated there.

== Descendants ==
*{{ill|Kusakabe-no-Masuhito|ja|日下部益人}}
*:A {{ill|Nara-period|ja|奈良時代}} regional gōzoku. Granted the surname Izu no Kuni no Miyatsuko Izu-no-Atai.<ref>Kotobank, "Kusakabe-no-Masuhito" [https://kotobank.jp/word/日下部益人-1071446]</ref>
*{{ill|Izu-no-Omina|ja|伊豆乎美奈}}
*:A Nara-period official, Junior Fifth Rank Lower.
